subject: Security exhibit orchestration: SOC 2 scope, pen-test windows, and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Alice Taggart <alice@acme-hs.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-hs.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit / audit rights - initial ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we are finalizing the order form and need to confirm the security exhibit language so our procurement and infosec teams can sign off. Two quick asks:

1) SOC 2: can you confirm which services and control boundaries Redwood intends to include in your SOC 2 scope for this contract? We need a one-paragraph statement we can put into our risk register (in-scope systems, data stores, and managed vs. customer-managed components).

2) Pen test & audit rights: we need the expected cadence (how often a third-party pen test will be performed), the requested windows for on-site/remote testing, and any constraints around sampling/production traffic. Also please include the evidence cadence for the most commonly requested artifacts (SaaS audit logs, change-control records, infra diagrams).

Ideally we can get a short statement and a suggested evidence handoff schedule this week so our legal team can avoid redlines. I attached our standard questionnaire for context.

Best,
Alice
Director, Information Security
Acme Health Systems

Attachment: Acme-questionnaire-2027.xlsx (referenced)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Taggart <alice@acme-hs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights - initial ask

Alice — thanks for the clear asks, appreciate the questionnaire. Quick summary below; Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Security/Infra) are looped for detail and sign-off.

SOC 2 scope (summary for your risk register):
- In-scope: Redwood hosted inference control plane (hosted API), model serving runtime for dedicated clusters (Redwood Dedicated), and the Redwood Console (observability/ops).
- Out-of-scope: customer-managed private deployment infrastructure (on-prem VMs/VPC subnets), and any customer-provided model art or data stored only in customer-managed storage.
- Evidence sources: SOC 2 report covers control design and operating effectiveness for the hosted control plane; supporting artifacts include audit logs/retention policies, change-management tickets, and encryption/key management descriptions.

Pen test & audit rights (proposed):
- Cadence: annual third-party penetration test for hosted services; additionally, we run quarterly internal security scans and triage.
- Windowing: we can schedule a 5-business-day remote testing window with a 2-week advance notice. For high-impact interactive tests (e.g., load-sustaining exploits), we require a read-only/limited sandbox or agreed time windows to avoid production disruption.
- Data/sample constraints: production traffic sampling only with mutually-agreed scope; Redwood will not provide raw PII data for pen-test use — we can provide realistic test datasets or scoped access with logging.

Evidence cadence (suggested handoff schedule):
- Week 0 (contract signing): SOC 2 report (summary) and high-level architecture diagram.
- Week 2: Access to logs metadata and retention statement; statement of key management (KMS/HSM) integrations.
- Quarterly: Pen-test summary and remediation log (redacted where necessary).
- On-request (business days, 3-5 business day SLA): specific artifacts such as change tickets, incident timeline, or narrowed audit logs (subject to legal/POC).

Attachments I’m sharing for your legal team: SOC2-2026-summary.pdf and pen-test-statement-redwood.docx.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the pen-test window constraints and whether Legal should expect any non-negotiable wording (e.g., restriction on on-site access or East/West region limitations)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if it helps.

—Vanessa
Director, Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-2026-summary.pdf; pen-test-statement-redwood.docx

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Taggart <alice@acme-hs.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights - initial ask

Thanks Vanessa — confirmed on high level. A few legal notes we should bake into the order form/security exhibit to avoid protracted redlines:

- Limit audit rights to evidence and reasonable requests: propose language that allows for document inspection and access to redacted logs, but not broad, continuous access to live systems. We should provide a predefined list of example artifacts instead of open-ended "all logs."
- Pen-test constraints: require a scoped test plan and one-week notice for any active exploit attempts. Add a clause that requires mutual escalation and an agreed remediation window (30 days for severity >= High) before any public disclosure.
- Confidentiality and non-production data: ensure the exhibit explicitly states Redwood will not provide raw customer PII for testing and that any shared artifacts will be redacted or replaced with synthetic data.

I will draft suggested exhibit language and ping Legal’s contract owner. Karthik — if you can confirm the 5-business-day window and whether we need to include region-specific exceptions (APAC customers sometimes require additional approvals).

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Taggart <alice@acme-hs.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights - initial ask

Vanessa / Marissa / Karthik — this is helpful, thank you. A couple clarifying points from our procurement team:

- The one-week notice for active exploit attempts is acceptable; procurement will want the 30-day remediation window language.
- For SOC 2 we only need a concise statement of scope and the most recent report; we will not ask for continuous log access. That should keep legal review quick.
- Please include a sample evidence checklist (just the list of artifact names and cadence) in the order form appendix — we can reference that rather than enumerating in the MSA body.

If you can send a short exhibit draft and the sample checklist by end of day Friday (28 May), procurement will start redline review. If anything blocks that delivery, flag here and we’ll be flexible on the timing.

Best,
Alice
